chapter: Buck's Legion band and later gigs
title: 1950 tapes at the American Legion hall
summary: Recollection of students taping the band at the Plum Plant Legion hall and who came to listen.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: I got it on my mind. Yeah. Do you remember there were some kids from Florida, I think, in the radio, a studying radio or something, and they made some tapes up here back in 1950 at American Legion at the Plum Plant. No, I think you don't. And I wonder whatever happened to those tapes. I'd love to find that again. I like to hear that. I like to get the light, get a copy of it. They were friends of Don Harris.
Yeah, I remember Don. I saw him last night.

He's doing okay. He's working at WDSU TV. Is it late? Yeah, he runs a motion picture projector and stuff. You know, he was always like tape machines and motion picture projectors and stuff like that. So he's there. I saw him last night and he might have to tell us what happened to those kids. And who came to the American Legion there? I mean, we had Don and me and a few people. Nick. Who? Nick?
Nick, what was his name? Stuck at the G. Gagliano?
Yeah. Yeah, he liked it. Yeah.
And a lot of musicians came out there.
Jazz fans, some jazz fans. Yeah, Harry Shields, he came out there like.
I'm like, you know, Fugirot, Almarico. But most of the people that just came to that, just from neighborhoods, from uptown, downtown, over the river.
They came from all over. And then the war broke out.
